name: India Wants to Build the Machines That Build India

fields.YouTube title: India’s ₹11,000 Crore Push to Build Construction Equipment
fields.YouTube description (includes hashtags):
India wants to manufacture more of the machines that build its infrastructure.

On 25 November 2026, the Union Cabinet approved a ₹11,000 crore scheme to strengthen India's construction and infrastructure equipment manufacturing ecosystem. It targets advanced machinery such as tunnel boring machines, excavators, off-highway trucks and cranes, as well as critical components including engines, transmissions and hydraulic systems.

India is the world's third-largest construction equipment market, with estimated import dependence of around 45%. Under the new scheme, eligible equipment manufacturers can receive incentives of up to 13% on qualifying incremental sales. The programme also supports a planned domestic testing facility.

The government expects ₹21,000 crore in investment. These are approved scheme provisions and projected outcomes, not investment or production already achieved.
